title: Smart telemetry ingest arbitration for Prometheus and OTLP with latency anchors
creator: Marcus Li
description: Create a protocol-aware intake arbitration layer that normalizes and routes Prometheus scrape payloads and OTLP metric batches into a unified KPI stream for inference metrics. The goal is to preserve high-cardinality model/route labels, maintain accurate per-request latency anchors for SLOs, reduce duplicate token-cost attributions, and provide graceful backpressure for Dedicated and Edge collectors.
problem_statement: We currently ingest Prometheus and OTLP telemetry via separate pipelines that diverge in label schemas, latency attribution, and sampling behavior. This causes mismatched KPIs in the console (per-route P95 differences), duplicated attribution for multi-protocol clients, and operational complexity when rolling out metric schema changes. We need a single arbitration layer to: (1) canonicalize labels, (2) attach deterministic latency anchors for each inference request, (3) apply consistent sampling & dedup rules, and (4) route metrics to the appropriate downstream (prom-rollup storage, SLO engine, and long-term analytics).
technical_design:
The arbitration layer sits between collectors (edge sidecar / ingress OTLP) and downstream processors. Key elements:
- Protocol adapters: lightweight adapters that convert Prometheus scrape / remote_write and OTLP/metrics into a canonical envelope. Each adapter emits: metric_name, timestamp (ns), canonical_labels, source_id, and request_context_id (if available).
- Deterministic request_context_id: use a stable hash of available identifiers (trace_id, request_id, model_id, route) when a direct trace link exists; fallback to a tenant+sampled-sampler token. The request_context_id is used to aggregate per-request latency anchors.
- Latency anchors: on trace-linked requests, emit a synthetic histogram bucket anchor with fixed boundaries so SLO rollups compute consistent quantiles across protocols.
- Deduplication layer: idempotency keys derived from request_context_id + metric fingerprint to drop duplicate metrics from multi-protocol exports.
- Backpressure & admission control: token-bucket per-tenant with priority lanes for P99-sensitive routes; soft-fallthrough policy to enrich instead of drop when safe.
- Schema contract module: validates canonical_labels (required: tenant_id, model_family, model_version, route, hw_tier) and emits a reject/rewrite telemetry metric for malformed payloads.
- Downstream routing: rules to fanout to fast-rollup store for console SLOs, compressed cold store for analytics, and alerting pipeline for error/latency spikes.
Implementation notes: Golang service with high-throughput non-blocking processors. Use capnproto for envelope encoding on the wire; pluggable adapters for future protocols (gRPC OTLP v2, prometheus remote write v1/v2).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical envelope accepted by downstream rollup service and console shows matching per-route P95 vs OTLP-only baseline within 1%
Deduplication prevents >95% of duplicate points when both Prometheus and OTLP export the same request
Latency anchors available in console SLO dashboards for 99% of trace-linked requests
Admission control reduces peak ingestion rate during edge storms without losing high-priority routes
Schema contract emits monitoring metrics and a reviewable daily report for label drift
rollout_plan: Deploy arbitration as beta region-only (us-west-2) behind feature flag
Enable OTLP->arbitration path for a single high-traffic tenant (telemetry-testing) for 48h
Enable Prometheus remote_write path for same tenant and monitor dedup metrics/console SLOs
Gradually enable for more tenants and switch default routing after 2 weeks of stable metrics
Fallback: toggle routing to bypass arbitration if error rate > 0.5% or P95 deviation > 5%
testing_plan: Unit tests for adapters and schema contract
Load test scenario: 100k QPS of metric writes with mixed OTLP/scrape payloads to validate dedup and admission control
Chaos test: simulate edge-sidecar duplicate delivery and network reordering to validate idempotency
End-to-end validation: synthetic traces and metrics with known latencies to assert console P50/P95 stability
Canary with production sample and automated rollback on SLO regression
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Incorrect canonicalization could break downstream dashboards. Mitigation: additive mode (emit canonical copy without deleting original stream for 2 weeks)
Risk: New service becomes ingestion bottleneck. Mitigation: horizontal shard by tenant and source_id; pre-warm with synthetic traffic
Risk: Label drift leads to high-cardinality explosion. Mitigation: reject/rewrite policy with daily drift reports and autosuggest remappings
Risk: Backpressure impacting critical customers. Mitigation: reserve priority lanes and surge credits for enterprise tenants
notes: Design reviewed with Observability and Serving runtime teams on 2026-02-25. Action: add hw_tier to canonical labels for routing to Dedicated pools.
Prototype showed 2.3x reduction in duplicate count for a mixed exporter test across 3 tenants.
We should align label naming with Console-2026.02 schema before wide rollout. PM: Camille Rios to approve mapping.
